page: Microsoft Azure D48alds_v6 is an x86_64 architecture server powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running at 3.7 GHz. This virtual machine features 48 vCPUs mapped to 24 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is configured with 96.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The hardware configuration includes 2835 GB of local storage and supports Premium Storage, though it does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark evaluations, the AMD EPYC processor delivers strong performance, placing in the top 25% for both single-core and multi-core stress-ng tests, as well as Geekbench and Passmark CPU suites. Memory performance is split, showing strong cached read-only bandwidth at 3648.29 GB/sec, but dropping to average tiers for uncached large-block read and write operations. The server demonstrates high-efficiency execution in database operations, with Redis SET operations reaching 66.39 million operations per second.

The primary tradeoff of this instance is its low memory-to-CPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core, which limits its suitability for memory-bound applications. This limitation is reflected in LLM inference benchmarks, where text generation for a large 70B model falls into the bottom 10% at 2.56 tokens per second, whereas smaller 135M model text generation reaches top-tier speeds. Given the high compute density and substantial local storage, this server is suited for compute-intensive workloads, software compilation, database operations, and localized data processing that do not require massive memory footprints.

With a low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core, this instance is designed for compute-heavy tasks rather than memory-intensive applications. Benchmarks indicate strong CPU performance, placing in the top 25% for multi-core processing, software compilation, and database operations, with Redis SET operations reaching 66.39 million operations per second. However, memory bandwidth for uncached large blocks remains average, and large-scale LLM text generation is a notable bottleneck, scoring in the bottom 10% for 70B models. This server is suited for compute-intensive workloads, software development pipelines, and database operations requiring fast local storage.
